evidence: Diagnostic of archived lunar CM1 simulations at kilometre resolution, conditioned on cold snow-bearing cells, plus independent sub-metre turbulence scenarios. Neither empirical lunar validation nor a prediction of giant-flake survival or resort weather.
reading_rule: Keep each run separate. The two full-cycle boxes use different microphysics and the third is a selected storm window, not an occurrence sample. Summaries weight sampled cell-times equally. The snow mask describes local model snow mass, not flakes crossing a surface. Grid-scale velocities and gradients are not dissipation estimates. Epsilon scenarios cannot be assigned to sampled cloud cells without an additional closure.

literature.citation: Chellini and Kneifel (2024), Turbulence as a Key Driver of Ice Aggregation and Riming in Arctic Low-Level Mixed-Phase Clouds, GRL 51, e2023GL106599
literature.read_scope: Publisher abstract and plain-language summary, not a full methodological review
literature.used_for: Terrestrial mixed-phase cloud anchor: changes in aggregation, particle number and riming accompany dissipation moving from below 1e-4 to above 1e-3 m2/s3. These rates are not lunar measurements.
literature.scenario_choice: 1e-4 and 1e-3 m2/s3 bracket the published transition; 1e-5 and 1e-2 extend sensitivity one decade each way. The extension is our scenario choice, not a reported lunar or terrestrial interval.

literature.citation: Koetsche et al. (2026), Snow microphysical processes in orographic turbulence revealed by cloud radar and in situ snowfall camera observations, ACP 26, 3277-3297
literature.read_scope: Abstract and section 2.5 on the turbulence retrieval; 26 August 2026 corrigendum read in full
literature.corrigendum_effect: Corrects reflectivity-difference units, a figure caption and acknowledgements; the dissipation threshold and conclusions used here are unchanged.
literature.used_for: An Earth orographic snowfall study identifies turbulent layers using a 1e-3 m2/s3 dissipation threshold. Its observations support treating enhanced aggregation and fragmentation together; it does not establish an aerodynamic size cap for lunar flakes.

literature.citation: Kolmogorov (1941), The local structure of turbulence in incompressible viscous fluid for very large Reynolds numbers; English republication (1991), Proc. R. Soc. A 434, 9-13
literature.read_scope: English republication, local-isotropy and similarity derivation
literature.used_for: Locally isotropic small-scale similarity. Our prefactor-one velocity increment is a dimensional estimate, not a calibrated RMS statistic or a model of intermittent extremes.

cm1_source_audit.finding: cm1setup=2 and ipbl=2 call the Bryan-Rotunno diagnostic vertical Smagorinsky closure. These runs have sgsmodel=0 and do not prognose LES TKE. restart_write.F writes tkea only when idoles and iusetke are true, and writes MYNN/MYJ 3-D variables only for ipbl=4,5,6. Thus missing output_tke is not the only obstacle: switching that output on alone cannot recover a prognostic cloud TKE field in the selected configuration.
cm1_source_audit.limits: Grid-scale velocities can be recovered. Direct dissipation, a resolved inertial-range spectrum, centimetre-to-metre gust increments and snow-aggregate mechanical strength cannot be recovered from these archived outputs. The closure includes vertical mixing; sgsmodel=0 does not mean the simulation has no mixing.

sources.redistribution: Only citations, short paraphrases and source hashes are stored here. No outside paper or dataset bytes are redistributed.

cases.selected_byte_rule: For each output: little-endian int32 level indices, then each FIELDS name plus NUL and its little-endian float32 array in C order (z,y,x) at those levels.

sampling.method: Nearest equally spaced indices across available outputs after from_day; no storm selection within a case. The storms_second case itself is a preselected active window.

layer_depths_in_snowy_columns.reading_rule: For each sampled column holding cold snow >=0.01 g/kg, maximum contiguous depth among flagged -20..0 C cells at 20-60 km. Environment masks need not themselves contain snow. Cell boundaries define depth; 2-km cells cannot locate thinner layers, and persistence along a flake trajectory is not measured. Zeros retained for snowy columns lacking that environment.

scenarios.evidence: Uncalibrated scenarios. Epsilon is imposed, not recovered from CM1; no probabilities or lunar turbulence classes are assigned. No bond strength or breakup criterion is fitted.

reference_geometry.evidence: Fixed representative area sensitivity: q(1024)*phi(1024) from synthetic dendrites aggregates. Holding this ratio at all sizes and combining it with Brown–Francis is a modelling scenario, not a habit-specific mass fit. Earth cloud aggregate relation; not validated for 0.15–0.60 m snow. No riming, crystal habit fractions or geometric scatter represented.

formulas.dynamic_pressure: rho (delta_u)^2 / 2; loading scale only, not tensile stress on a branch
formulas.aligned_slip_pressure_increment: rho V delta_u + rho (delta_u)^2 / 2, from changing settling slip V to V+delta_u. An adverse aligned fluctuation envelope, not actual spatial stress or an intermittent maximum. Assumes unchanged drag coefficient.

scenarios.reading_rule: D must be within an approximately isotropic locally equilibrated cascade. At D below the Kolmogorov length the smooth-gradient expression is used. Mean translation does not enter these increments. No survival claim follows by comparing pressure with weight: contacts, drag fluctuations, flutter and collisions need separate mechanical laws.
